newsitem.title: USA: Shopko, Phar-Mor terminate merger agreement.
newsitem.headline: Shopko, Phar-Mor terminate merger agreement.

text.p: Retailer ShopKo Stores Inc. and retail drug chain Phar-Mor Inc. said Wednesday they called off their planned $1 billion merger.
The companies, which announced the proposed merger in September, said in a joint statement that they cancelled the proposed deal because of "continuing uncertainties" that they did not specify.

The companies, which have combined annual sales of $3.2 billion, agreed in September to merge by creating a holding company that was to be called Cabot Noble, with each of the two companies continuing to operate separately as subsidiaries.

ShopKo, based in Green Bay, Wis., operates 130 stores in 15 states stretching from the upper Midwest to the Pacific Northwest. Its ProVantage Inc. unit specialises in prescription, vision and health benefit services.
Youngstown, Ohio-based Phar-Mor operates 103 retail drug stores in 18 states, concentrated around Ohio, Pennsylvania and Virginia.

"While we continue to believe that a strategic combination would make sense, it became clear that the transaction as contemplated was not likely to be completed and that the continuing uncertainty is not in the best interests of our shareholders," Dale P. Kramer, chief executive officer of ShopKo, said in the statement.
"We will continue to pursue other strategic opportunities that will allow us to build on our market position and enhance the Phar-Mor concept," Phar-Mor Chairman Robert Haft said.
